api_definitions.labeling:
- `env.mission`: the mission string, for example `pick up the grey box`. Mission targets
  come from it: do not assume a fixed color or object, match the designated one.
- `env.agent_pos`: the agent position as `(x, y)`.
- `env.agent_dir`: the facing direction as `0` right, `1` down, `2` left, `3` up.
- `env.grid.get(x, y)`: the object at that cell, or `None` when the cell is empty. Grid
  coordinates use `0 <= x < env.width` and `0 <= y < env.height`.
- Object attributes: `type` (for example `key`, `door`, `box`, `ball`, `wall`, `goal`),
  `color`, and `is_open` and `is_locked` on doors. Door openness and lock state come from
  them.
- `env.carrying`: the carried object, or `None`; it exposes `type` and `color`. Carry state
  comes from it.
- `env.width`, `env.height`: grid size.

Object classes cannot be imported. To scan the grid, guard empty cells with
`cell is not None` before reading an attribute. This expression checks whether any cell holds
a given object type:

    any(cell is not None and cell.type == "<type>" for x in range(env.width) for y in range(env.height) for cell in [env.grid.get(x, y)])

inputs.environment_markdown:
# MiniGrid DoorKey

## Environment

The agent starts on one side of a wall. A locked yellow door separates it from the green goal, and a matching yellow key is accessible on the starting side. The agent has seven actions: turn left, turn right, move forward, pick up, drop, toggle, and done. Done does nothing. The layout and initial pose change between resets.

Layout: a square grid of N x N cells with an outer wall; N is 5, 6, 8 or 16 depending on the variant. A wall spans the full height at a random column and has one gap, the locked yellow door, at a random row. The agent starts left of the wall, the yellow key lies on the left side, and the goal sits in the bottom-right inner corner. Nothing else is in the grid. The mission text is always "use the key to open the door and then get to the goal".

## Objective and episode boundary

The task is complete when the agent reaches the goal after using the key to unlock and open the door. The environment ends the episode on reaching the goal and cuts it at the step limit. Its success reward is 1 minus 0.9 times the fraction of the step limit used.

The step limit is 10 times N squared (640 for N = 8). The step that moves the agent onto the goal ends the episode, so no step follows `at_goal`.

## Proposition semantics

These are state conditions evaluated at every time point.

| id | kind | true when |
|---|---|---|
| `has_key` | condition | the agent carries the yellow key |
| `door_open` | condition | the door is open; false again if the door is toggled shut |
| `at_goal` | condition, last step only | the agent stands on the goal cell |
| `key_lost` | event, reading | `has_key` was true at the previous step, is false now, and `door_open` is false now; false on every other step |

`key_lost` reading: the description does not say whether it is an event or lingers. This file reads it as an event. Both readings agree while the agent holds the key. They differ only after the key is dropped: the event is true for that one step, not until the key is picked up again.

## Constraints

- `door_open` cannot become true before `has_key`: only toggling with the yellow key in hand unlocks the door.
- `at_goal` cannot become true before `door_open`: the wall has no other gap.
- `key_lost` and `door_open` never hold together: the event requires the door not open.
- `key_lost` and `has_key` never hold together: the event requires the key not carried.
- `key_lost` and `at_goal` never hold together: `key_lost` needs a drop step and `at_goal` a forward step.

## What the agent can and cannot do

- Can: turn; move forward onto an empty cell, an open door or the goal; pick up the key with empty hands; drop onto an empty cell in front; toggle the door in front.
- Cannot: walk through a closed or locked door; unlock without the yellow key in hand (toggle then does nothing); pick up the door, walls or goal; drop onto an occupied cell; relock a door.
- Reaching the goal does not require dropping the key. The step onto the goal ends the episode, so `at_goal` is the last step.
- `door_open` can turn false again: toggling an unlocked door shuts it. Nothing relocks it.
- Unlocking does not use up the key, so `has_key` stays true after `door_open` unless the agent drops it. Dropping it then is not `key_lost`, because the door is open.
- `key_lost` can fire more than once while the door stays closed: pick the key up, drop it, pick it up, drop it.

## Example trace

A real episode on the 8 x 8 grid: 17 steps, reward 0.976.

1. 2 turns and moves, no proposition changes
2. `pickup` (step 3): `has_key` true
3. 6 turns and moves, no proposition changes
4. `toggle` (step 10): `door_open` true
5. 6 turns and moves, no proposition changes
6. `forward` (step 17): `at_goal` true [episode terminated]

Variant, a second real episode: `pickup` (step 7): `has_key` true. `drop` (step 8): `has_key` false, `key_lost` true. `pickup` (step 9): `has_key` true, `key_lost` false.

## Propositions
- `has_key`: The agent is currently carrying the yellow key that opens the locked door.
- `door_open`: The separating yellow door is currently open.
- `at_goal`: The agent is currently on the green goal tile.
- `key_lost`: The agent previously acquired the yellow key but is no longer carrying it before opening the door.

## Example tasks

- Eventually acquire the key.
- Open the door after acquiring the key.
- Reach the goal after opening the door.


# MiniGrid DoorKey: code notes

Addition to `environment.md`; read both. Facts live there; this file says where they come from and how code reads them.

## Source and runtime

- Official source: <https://github.com/Farama-Foundation/Minigrid>
- ARM-FM artifacts: <https://github.com/roger-creus/llms-rm-rl/tree/main/reward_machines/DoorKey>
- Gymnasium IDs: `MiniGrid-DoorKey-5x5-v0`, `MiniGrid-DoorKey-6x6-v0`, `MiniGrid-DoorKey-8x8-v0`, and `MiniGrid-DoorKey-16x16-v0`. Recommended default: `MiniGrid-DoorKey-8x8-v0`.
- Runtime: `minigrid==3.1.0`, `gymnasium==1.3.0`, pinned in `requirements.txt`.
- `[code: file:function]` is MiniGrid 3.1.0 source (`minigrid/...`). `[run: script]` is a scripted run or check on the real environment, with `doorkey.py`, `layout_checks.py` or `mechanics_check.py`.

## Truth conditions in code

`prev` is `env.episode_memory["previous_valuation"]`; at the first step every proposition is false in it. `H` and `D` stand for the `has_key` and `door_open` expressions. There is one door, so a scan by type finds it.

| id | expression |
|---|---|
| `has_key` | `env.carrying is not None and env.carrying.type == "key" and env.carrying.color == "yellow"` |
| `door_open` | `any(c is not None and c.type == "door" and c.is_open for x in range(env.width) for y in range(env.height) for c in [env.grid.get(x, y)])` |
| `at_goal` | `any(c is not None and c.type == "goal" for c in [env.grid.get(*env.agent_pos)])` |
| `key_lost` | `prev["has_key"] and not H and not D` (event: previous step against the current state) |

## Evidence

Layout and mission text [code: doorkey.py:DoorKeyEnv._gen_grid; run: `layout_checks.py`, 300 seeds]. The seven actions and `done` doing nothing [code: minigrid_env.py:step].

- Environment, objective: step limit `10 * size**2` [code: doorkey.py:DoorKeyEnv.__init__]. Reward `1 - 0.9 * (step_count / max_steps)`: stock environment behavior, untagged in the previous file.
- Objective, `at_goal` is last: the step onto the goal ends the episode [code: minigrid_env.py:step; run: `mechanics_check.py`].
- Proposition semantics, `key_lost` reading: read as an event because the labeling code sees one step of memory and the project's labeling prompt treats `key_lost` as an event. The published RM uses it only from the has-key state [`task-rm-pairs.md:15`]. Fired in 94 of 300 random episodes [run: `doorkey.py`].
- Constraints, `door_open` after `has_key`: [code: world_object.py:Door.toggle; run: `doorkey.py`, 0 of 300 random episodes, 207 reached `door_open`].
- Constraints, `at_goal` after `door_open`: [code: doorkey.py:_gen_grid; run: `layout_checks.py`, goal unreachable without the door in 300/300 seeds].
- Constraints, `key_lost` with `door_open` and `has_key`: follow from the `key_lost` definition in the table of `environment.md`.
- Constraints, `key_lost` with `at_goal`: [code: minigrid_env.py:step; run: `doorkey.py`, 0 of 300].
- Can: [code: minigrid_env.py:step].
- Cannot: pick up the door, walls or goal [code: world_object.py:can_pickup]; drop onto an occupied cell, relock a door [run: `mechanics_check.py`]. Closed door and unlocking without the key: untagged in the previous file.
- Goal is the last step [code: minigrid_env.py:step].
- `door_open` can turn false again [code: Door.toggle; run: `mechanics_check.py`]. Nothing relocks it [code: Door sets `is_locked` only in `__init__` and `toggle`, and `toggle` only clears it].
- Key kept after unlocking, dropping it is not `key_lost` [run: `mechanics_check.py`].
- `key_lost` can repeat [code: `pickup`, `drop` in minigrid_env.py:step].
- Example trace: seed 0, `MiniGrid-DoorKey-8x8-v0`, scripted solver with privileged grid access [run: `doorkey.py`, log `doorkey_trace_seed0.jsonl`]. Variant: seed 1 [run: `doorkey.py`, log `doorkey_keylost_seed1.jsonl`].

- `env.carrying`: the carried object, or `None`; it exposes `type` and `color`. Carry state

- `env.width`, `env.height`: grid size.
